heading: Sharing alpha nodes
text:
### Sharing alpha nodes [IRET.6.6]

Two rules that have identical patterns on the same schema
with identical tests share one alpha node. The compiler
is responsible for deduplication; the RETP atom encodes
the node graph, including shared references. The loader
respects shared nodes — one in-memory `ds_rete_alpha_node_t`
may appear as the right input to multiple beta nodes.

---

idris.name: iret_6_6__alpha_at
idris.note: A beta node references its right alpha by position [RDSC.4a.3]; sharing is by reference.

idris.name: iret_6_6__alpha_or
idris.note: The node a reference resolves to; a dangling reference is a node admitting nothing. Its own function so a proof can reduce it by rewriting the lookup alone.

idris.name: iret_6_6__alpha_at_just
idris.note: A resolving reference yields its node.

idris.name: iret_6_6__alpha_at_nothing
idris.note: A dangling reference yields the node admitting nothing.

idris.name: iret_6_6__alpha_at_set_eq
idris.note: Updating the referenced node updates what the reference yields.

idris.name: iret_6_6__alpha_at_set_neq
idris.note: Updating another node leaves what the reference yields: sharing by reference is by position.

idris.name: iret_6_6__nth_beyond
idris.note: A position past the list resolves to nothing.
